source_text: Vae vobis Scribae et Pharisaei hypocritae, quia similes estis sepulcris dealbatis, quae a foris parent speciosa, intus plena ossibus mortuorum. Sic et vos a foris paretis justi, intus pleni hypocrisi et iniquitate. Omnis justitia simulata mortua justitia est.
orientation: Origen is commenting on Jesus' woe against the scribes and Pharisees, quoting Matthew 23:27-28 and then adding his own moral gloss.
pass_a_gloss: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you are like whitewashed tombs, which outside appear beautiful, but inside are full of the bones of the dead. So also you outside appear righteous, but inside are full of hypocrisy and iniquity. Every pretended righteousness is a dead righteousness.

choices.why: The glossary does not cover this term, but 'whitewashed tombs' is the standard literal rendering of the image and preserves the contrast between outward appearance and inward corruption.
The glossary requires 'pretended righteousness' for justitia simulata, and the literal lane must use the glossary English.
The glossary gives 'hypocrites' for hypocritae; the noun hypocrisis is rendered 'hypocrisy' to keep the same root and the moral sense of inward pretense.
The literal contrast between dead and living righteousness is the point of Origen's gloss, and 'dead righteousness' preserves the stark adjective-noun pairing.

pass_b_english: "Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you are like whitewashed tombs, which look beautiful on the outside but inside are full of the bones of the dead. So you also look righteous on the outside, but inside you are full of hypocrisy and lawlessness" (Matthew 23:27-28). Every pretended righteousness is a dead righteousness.
